cards.title: The story is one reducer with seven doors, not three booleans set at each
acceptance: turnReduce({stop:3, story:true, playing:true, epoch:e}, {type:'step', to:5}) -> stop 5, playing true, epoch e+1; then {type:'tick', epoch:e} -> state unchanged (a stale tick is dropped); {type:'tick', epoch:e+1} -> stop 6. Today a manual step while playing keeps the old setInterval, so the next auto-advance fires on that interval's leftover time, not a full beat after the step
{type:'toggle'} (the TURN button) from {story:false, playing:false} -> story true, playing false; again from {story:true, playing:true} -> story false, playing false
{type:'view', id:'lanes'} while playing -> story false, playing false; {type:'view', id:'turn'} -> story true, stop unchanged

{type:'tool', stop:'12', tell:false} while playing -> {stop:11, story:false, playing:false}; {type:'tool', stop:2.5} -> {ok:false, error:'No stop 2.5. The turn has 12 stops, numbered from 1.'} and the state is unchanged

{type:'play'} with env.reduced true -> stop+1 and playing stays false; and with state.playing true and reduced true, the selector playingNow(state, {reduced:true}) is false, so turnRead's `playing` reads false. Today read_turn reports playing:true while reduced motion has stopped the clock
{type:'step', to:-1} from stop 0 -> 11; {type:'step', to:12} -> 0; {type:'chapter', index:2} -> stop CHAPTER_VIEWS[2].from and epoch+1; {type:'pick', index:4} from story off -> story true, stop 4

Drawing.tsx (comments stripped) declares no useState for story, stop or playing and calls no setStop, setStory or setPlaying; Tools.tsx's set_turn handler makes exactly one dispatch and answers turnRead from the reduced state
every action keeps the invariants: 0 <= stop < 12, playing implies story, and an action that moves stop by hand increments epoch (a property loop over every action type from 8 seed states)

cards.body:
## Summary
The guided story's state (stop, story, playing) is three useStates written from seven places: the TURN toggle, the view bus, set_turn, the story bar's play/step/chapter, the editorial script rail and the interval tick. Each door re-states the rules (wrap the stop, playing implies story, reduced motion steps instead of playing) by hand. Move them into one pure `turnReduce(state, action, env)` in turn.ts, with an `epoch` so a tick from before a manual move is dropped. Drawing then uses useReducer, and Tools sends one dispatch.

## Description
This is client-state/status-fsms: flags combine into states nobody listed, so every illegal state has to be blocked at every write site. Two fixes have already landed for this class, one door at a time: b6f01d2b (set_turn tell=false did not stop the clock) and 7ad745d6 (a fractional stop crashed the story bar). Two defects are still live. (1) The tick is `setInterval` keyed on [beatMs, playing, reduced] (Drawing.tsx:288-292), not on the stop. So a manual step, chapter jump or set_turn while playing is followed by an auto-advance on the old interval's leftover time, and the beat the reader picked can flash past. This is client-state/async-race-guards: a stale producer overwrites a fresher choice. (2) Under reduced motion the clock is stopped but `playing` stays true, so read_turn (turn.ts:515) tells an agent the story is playing when nothing moves. The reducer makes `playing implies story` and `stop in range` impossible to break. It keeps every door's existing behaviour (cases 1, 2, 3 and 5 are guards), and turnAfter/askStop become thin calls of it.

## Flow
- turn.ts: StoryState {stop, story, playing, epoch}, an action union (toggle, view, tool, play, step, chapter, pick, tick), turnReduce, and playingNow(state, env); askStop and turnAfter are kept as wrappers so their tests stay green
- Drawing.tsx: useReducer replaces lines 170-172. The tick becomes a setTimeout keyed on [epoch, stop, playingNow], so each beat gets a full beatMs. Every handler becomes a dispatch
- Tools.tsx: set_turn sends one dispatch and answers turnRead(turnReduce(...)), which keeps the 'answer is the state it leaves' rule
- tests: lanes.turn.test.ts (cases 1-6 and 8), lanes.drawing.test.ts (case 7), lanes.poses.test.ts keeps the turnAfter cases

## Expected impact
A reader who steps while playing gets a full beat on the stop they picked. An agent's read_turn stops reporting a clock reduced motion has stopped. The next story door (deep link, keyboard shortcut, node-to-stop) is one action, not three more setter calls that can drift.

## Evaluation
Claim: the story's state has one transition authority, and the stale-tick and reduced-playing defects close
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (turnReduce does not exist; cases 1 and 5 describe live defects)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - the acceptance cases under node --test
Result: better
Gate: none
cards.evidence: Drawing.tsx:170-172 `const [story, setStory] = useState(false); const [stop, setStop] = useState(0); const [playing, setPlaying] = useState(false);`. Drawing.tsx:288-292 `useEffect(() => { if (!playing || reduced || beatMs <= 0) return; const id = setInterval(() => setStop((s) => (s + 1) % BEAT_VIEWS.length), beatMs); ... }, [beatMs, playing, reduced]);` - stop is not a dependency. Write sites: Drawing.tsx:266-269 (view onSet: setStory, setPlaying), :526-529 (pickStop: setStory, setStop with its own modulo), :559-562 (onStory: setStory, setPlaying), :660-664 (onPlay: setStop or setPlaying; onStep: its own modulo; onChapter: setStop), Tools.tsx:713-716 (turnAfter, then setStop, setStory, setPlaying). turn.ts:446-447 turnAfter keeps now.playing; turn.ts:515 turnRead returns `playing` as passed, and Tools passes the raw state (Tools.tsx:683). Chrome.tsx:258 shows 'Step' under reduced while `playing` may be true. git log: b6f01d2b 'set_turn tell=false stops the story clock, as the TURN toggle and the view switch do'; 7ad745d6 'set_turn refuses a fractional stop instead of crashing the story bar'.

cards.body:
## Summary
The drawing's fourteen runs are its claims, and each one is authored with a sentence (`note`) and a source (`cite`). No surface shows either: the runs are aria-hidden SVG on a plate with pointer-events none, read_turn sends only the label, and a node's spoken name says nothing about what it connects to. Make a run something you can open. Press it (an 8-px non-scaling hit stroke), or rove to it from a node with '[' and ']'. A readout then says its role, from and to, the note, the README section it cites, and which turn stops travel it. With the story on, opening a run jumps the story to the first stop it carries.

## Description
This is canvas-graph/edge-management, 'Interacting with edges': hit-test against a fat invisible stroke along the same path, and hang context off the selection. It is also canvas-graph/canvas-accessibility, 'expose the graph, not the geometry'. A reader now has to trust a line they cannot question. The readout also brings out a finding the drawing hides today: `e-approval`, a MAIN run labelled 'GATED · approval', carries no stop of the turn's script, because the script walks catalog -> contracts -> record. A reader who opens it sees 'no stop travels this run'. During the story it stays dimmed with no reason given (Drawing.tsx:409-413 reveals only hop edges). The pure module inspect.ts holds runReadout, runsTouching, cycleRun and selectRun, so node --test reaches every rule. Scene, Drawing and Chrome only render and route keys. nodeName gains its incoming and outgoing runs, so a screen-reader user can hear the graph. read_turn's edges gain note and cite, so an agent gets what a sighted reader now gets. Text stays secondary: one compact readout under the title band, the same slot the story bar uses, not a prose panel.

## Flow
- inspect.ts: runReadout(id), runsTouching(node), cycleRun(node, current, dir), selectRun(state, id), clearRun, all derived from EDGES, NODE_BY_ID, ROLE_LABEL and story HOPS (nothing re-typed)
- Scene.tsx: Runs draws a transparent .al-run-hit path per run with data-run-id and data-selected, and onSelect
- lanes.css: .al-plate keeps pointer-events none and .al-run-hit opts in with pointer-events: stroke; a selected run thickens; readout styles use existing tokens
- Drawing.tsx: `run` selection state; '[' and ']' on a focused node cycle its runs; Escape or a node open clears; selecting with the story on moves the stop (through the reducer if slot A lands first, through setStop otherwise)
- Chrome.tsx: RunReadout (role dot, from -> to, note, cite, 'carries stops 7' or 'no stop travels this run')
- workflow.ts nodeName and turn.ts turnRead gain the graph facts; tests as listed

## Expected impact
Every line on the sheet can be questioned where it is drawn. A reader can check a claim against its README section without leaving the canvas. Keyboard and screen-reader users get the edges for the first time. The one main run the turn never walks shows up instead of staying silent.

## Evaluation
Claim: all 14 runs are addressable by pointer, keyboard, screen reader and agent, and each answers its note, cite and carried stops
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (no inspect.ts; note and cite are rendered nowhere: grep finds no edge .note or .cite read in the variant)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - the acceptance cases under node --test
Result: better
Gate: none
cards.evidence: workflow.ts:418-420 `/** The longer reading, for the receipt and read_turn. */ note: string; cite: string;`, authored on all 14 EDGES (workflow.ts:441-612). grep -n '\.note\b|\.cite\b' over archify-lanes/ finds only lane, phase, chapter and beat note/cite reads (Chrome.tsx:241,251,288,331; turn.ts:83,110,116,122; workflow.ts:356 node note). No edge note or cite is read anywhere. turn.ts:509-514 read_turn edges = {hop, edge, role, label} with no note or cite. lanes.css:230-235 `.al-plate { ... pointer-events: none; }` and Scene.tsx:161-201 render the runs inside that plate with no handler; Scene.tsx:237 Trail is aria-hidden. workflow.ts:348-357 nodeName gives the lane, phase and note but no connections. Probe of story.ts HOPS: index 6 hooks->catalog edge e-class; 7 catalog->contracts null; 8 contracts->record null; 10 record->channels e-up; 11 channels->desktop e-home. So e-approval (catalog->record, role main) is on no hop.
